rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 LATEST UPDATE 2 NEW FEATURES 3 GOAL OF THE GAME 4 GLOSSARY 5 SETUP 6 GAMEPLAY 7 PLAYER TURN 8 DICE PLACEMENT RULES 9 COLLECTING POINTS 10 KARMA 11 BLACK DICE 12 GOLD/YELLOW DICE 13 GAME END 14 WINNER 15 SINGLE PLAYER MODE LATEST UPDATE Matching the score value to score slot number earns total of 7 points instead of 6. NEW FEATURES The karma earned during player's turn can reach 12 points. However, the overflow can only be used on player's turn. Any karma over 6 points will be lost when the turn is over. GOAL OF THE GAME The goal of the game is to seed, grow and harvest the best tomatoes from your tomato vines while trying to prevent other gardeners from doing the same. You accomplish this by seeding (placing a die on one of your open tomato tokens) your vines with the best/highest-scoring dice you rolled and giving the low-scoring dice to your opponents. Top ↑ GLOSSARY Bushel - the designated space to hold available dice that are not currently in play, on the score tracks or tomato vines. Tomato Token - the tomato shaped token on which seed dice are placed. Seed Dice - a dice that is placed on an empty tomato token. Tomato Vine - tomato token with a seed dice on it plus any attached dice that form a sequence or set of numbers. Karma - the amount of gratitude points earned by helping opponents score points - completing their tomato vine. Karma Heart - the token to mark the current karma level. Karma Track - the track showing current karma level. Score Track - the "diced" tomato track on which players place the seed dice from a completed tomato vine. Top ↑ SETUP Each player receives: 11 red dice 2 black dice 1 golden dice - Sunny Golden Hybrid variant 3 tomato tokens 6 golden stars - Dicey Tomato Rules variant 3 Karma bits - Karma Overload variant 1 karma heart 1 karma track 1 score track All players roll a single die to determine the first (and last) player. The player with the lowest die value will be the last player and receives the last player marker - ketchup splatter. The next player in the order of play (usually to the left) becomes the first player. All dice are transferred to the Bushel. Each player places the karma heart on karma track in position 3. The first player starts the game. Top ↑ GAMEPLAY The game play is simple. On their turn, active players pick 3 dice from the bushel and roll them. All rolled dice need to be distributed - either placed on an empty tomato as a seed or added to an existing vine. Dice can be placed in their play area or in the opponents' play areas. Players are allowed to try to influence the active player's placement decision. Dice that cannot be placed are passed to the next player as additional dice to roll. Completing opponent's tomato earns the active player karma. The number of karma earned depends on the value scored by the opponent (see KARMA ). Karma can be spent immediately after earning them or at any time during active player's turn. Game continues until a 6th tomato of any player is completed. That triggers the final round which means that after the last player had their turn the game will end. Top ↑ PLAYER TURN Pick 3 dice from the bushel Roll the dice For each rolled dice Place dice following the DICE PLACEMENT RULES Use karma to change dice value or clear vines Earn karma for completing opponents' vine Collect points for completing own vines Pass any dice impossible to place. End turn Top ↑ DICE PLACEMENT RULES All rolled dice have to be placed if there is a valid spot for them to go to. They can be placed on any player's tomato vine either as a seed dice - placed on an empty open tomato token - or added to the tomato vine - must follow number sequence or set. Black dice can only be added to a vine, they cannot be used as seed dice. See BLACK DICE . Gold dice can only be added to a vine, they cannot be used as seed dice. See GOLD/YELLOW DICE . -- Example: -- Token 1: empty Token 2: 1 Token 3: 1,2 -- Actions -- Player rolls 1,2,3 Player can add 1 to Token 2 to form a set of 1s. Player can also place 1 on Token 1 as a seed dice. Player can place 3 on Token 1 and add 2 and 1 to form a sequence. The order could also be reversed or the seed could be a 2 with 1 below and 3 above the seed. Player could also add 2 and 3 to Token 2. Lastly, player can add 3 to Token 3. Top ↑ COLLECTING POINTS Main source of points in the game are the tomato vines. Additional points are scored at the end of the game from unused karma and unfinished tomato vines. Points from tomato vines - When a tomato vine has 4 dice it can be harvested - the owner of the vine transfers the seed dice from the tomato token of the vine onto their next available score spot and the remaining dice back to the bushel. The score is adjusted by number of black and golden dice on the vine. Each black dice lowers the score by 1 point. Each golden dice raises the score by 1 point. DICEY TOMATO RULES Variant When the score matches the score slot number, bonus points are awarded to make the score equal 7 points. So, if you score a 1 on score slot 1 you receive 6 bonus points and if you score 4 on score slot 4 you receive 3 bonus points. Also, the score slot is decorated with a gold star. Points for finishing the 6th tomato first - 2 points. Points from unused karma - each 2 unused karma points earn 1 end game point. Points from uncollected red dice on vines - each 3 red dice earn 1 point. Top ↑ KARMA Karma is the amount of gratitude players earn by helping other players score points. When an active player completes opponent's tomato - places the 4th dice on the vine - they earn karma points based on the score earned by the receiving player. ORIGINAL RULES 1 & 2 points earn 1 karma 3 & 4 points earn 2 karma 5 & 6 points earn 3 karma KARMA OVERLOAD VARIANT earn karma equal to opponent's score (without any bonuses) Each time you place one of your dice on opponent's vines and for each dice you pass to your opponent you receive karma bit. When you collect 3 bits you gain 1 karma. Karma can be used to: Re-Roll a single dice - costs 1 karma (when you click the "Restart" button after re-rolling the game will be restored to after the last re-roll) Shift rolled dice value - costs 2 karma Clean the vine - costs 3 karma Roll over dice (from 1 to 6 or from 6 to 1) - costs 4 karma Flip seed dice (6->1, 1->6, 5->2, 2->5, 3->4, 4->3) - costs 5 karma Change any rolled dice to any value - costs 6 karma Each 2 karma earns 1 point at the end of the game. Top ↑ BLACK DICE The "rotten" black dice can be used offensively and defensively. Players can use them to lower opponent's score by adding a black die to the tomato vine following the placement rules. They can also use them defensively to cancel/clear a tomato vine - if a tomato vine is worth 0 points at the end of active player's turn, that vine can be cleared (all dice, including the seed dice, return to the bushel). So if player has a seed dice worth 1 point, they can add black dice with value of either 1 or 2 which will lower the vine score to 0. Black dice can only be added to a vine, they cannot be used as seed dice. Top ↑ GOLD/YELLOW DICE Available in the Sunny Golden Hybrid game variant The "Sunny Golden Hybrid" gold/yellow are used to raise the value of the vine. Players also use them defensively to cancel/clear a tomato vine - if a tomato vine is worth more than 6 points at the end of active player's turn, that vine is overripe and has to be cleared (all dice, including the seed dice, return to the bushel). So if an opponent has a set of 3 6s on the vine, active player can add golden dice with value of 6 which will raise the vine score to 7 and make it overripe. As is the case with the black dice, golden dice can only be added to a vine, they cannot be used as seed dice. Top ↑ GAME END The final round is triggered when a 6th tomato of any player has been harvested. Game continues until the last player finishes their turn. When the last player distributes all their rolled dice the game ends. It is possible to end the game in a tie. Game also ends immediately if there are no dice in the bushel at the start of a player's turn. Top ↑ WINNER The winner of the game is the player with the most points from the tomato score track, unused karma and unfinished vines. Top ↑ SINGLE PLAYER MODE In single mode, your goal is to score all 6 tomatoes while matching the value scored to the score track number. So for the first score you want to get 1, for the second score you want to get 2, etc. Each matching score gives you a positive victory point. If you run out of dice without completing all 6 tomatoes you loose. But since single player can only be played in training mode you don't lose any prestige. The single mode was created for individuals to learn how the randomness of the dice can be manipulated through the use of karma and black dice. You earn karma hearts for each completed tomato based on the seed value as in the regular game except you earn it by completing your own tomatoes. The game does not end when there are no dice in the bushel as long as you still have dice in hand. Top ↑

[Rating: 3/10] Each turn you roll 3 new dice and allocate them to anyone’s sets. The aim is to construct sets of 4 dice, same number or in sequence, which will score points (when complete) equal to the first die placed in that set. What the game boils down to is roll high. Lock in high start dice in your sets and add to and complete them as quickly as you can. if you roll low, start sets for other players so they're forced to finish low-scoring sets. It was different for a roll and write but there is potential for a fair bit of take that and that isn't very pleasant when you get kicked when you're down. :-)  That can be forced to happen depending on the black die roll even if your opponent was hoping to get a different opponent - they obviously won't place the black die on their own board!

[Rating: 3/10] A game this simple needs at least adorable anthropomorphised vegetables to make it worth playing!

[Rating: 3/10] BGA - the game is missed one thing or two. The karma system feels awkward and out of theme, the option to pick which dice before roll is questionable - It still has potential, maybe with I Cut, You Choose or something to do with Roll and Write  Digital Implementation: Works well on mobile.

[Rating: 3/10] Diced Tomatoes needs some fine tuning. Optimal play is not obvious at first, which is generally good, but this is mostly due to opaque rules rather than a skill curve. Generally, you want to place high valued seed dice (or give opponents low valued seeds), although you can score a bit higher if you score a precise number. This latter option, while more lucrative, is much harder to achieve and does not seem to be worth the risk, especially since other players can more easily upend this strategy. All told the capacity for negative player interaction is way out of balance for this type of game. I

[Rating: 3/10] BGA seems like a great way to get your indie game some players. But is what your game needs a steady stream of players with no real investment in your game, comparing it to some of their favorite games? I'm not sure that situation was favorable to Diced Tomatoes, which I remember nothing about except that the choices weren't very interesting and I won without trying.

[Rating: 3/10] Dice chucker game with some interaction but just not exciting at all and very few interesting decisions to be made.

[Rating: 3.5/10] BGA - Not-so-clever push your luck dice game. Yeah, you can sort of manipulating the dice if you have the right energy to help with the roll, but most of the time you don't have that and try to mess with the other players. Not much going on and not a game I would care to play again.
